thick bakery style chocolate chip cookies🍪🍫 Ingredients: 170g (3/4 cup) unsalted butter, cold and cubed 150g (3/4 cup) brown sugar 70g (1/3 cup) granulated sugar 1 egg + 1 egg yolk 2 tsp vanilla 300g (2 1/2 cups) all purpose flour 1 tbsp cornstarch 1/2 tsp baking soda 1/4 tsp baking powder 3/4 tsp salt 250g (1 1/2 cups) chocolate chips  Flakey sea salt (optional) Instructions:  1. In a large bowl, combine the butter, brown sugar, and white sugar. Mix until smooth and well combined. Do not cream. 2. Add the egg, egg yolk, and vanilla, then mix until fully incorporated. 3. Add the dry ingredients (flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda, and salt) and fold until just combined. 4. Fold in the chocolate chips or chunks until evenly distributed. Do not overmix. 5. Divide the dough into 150g portions and shape each into a rough ball. 6. Place the dough balls on a lined tray, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight. 7. Bake in a preheated 190°C (375°F) oven for 13-16 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the centers are still slightly soft. 8. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking tray for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. If desired, sprinkle with flaky sea salt and let cool for about 15 minutes before serving. Enjoy! Note: This recipe made 6 cookies weighing 150g each and 1 cookie weighing 100g🍪🤎 #baking #cookies #chocolatechipcookies #Recipe #nyccookies

Kohakutou - Japanese Crystal Candy 🍬  If you’ve seen people buying the Silky Gem brand of these candies…I need you to know how cheap it is to just make them yourself at home. Recipe below! Ingredients: ½ cup water  1 tsp agar agar powder (3g) 1 cup sugar (215g) Flavor (e.g. lychee in this video)  Food coloring 1. Dissolve agar agar powder in water and bring to a simmer and stirring til dissolved.  2. Add in sugar, stir until dissolved and then mix in your desired flavouring. Simmer (small bubbles) for about 5 minutes until it thickens into a syrupy texture. Be careful not to over boil (it will spill over and make a mess). 3. Pour into a square or rectangular heat resistant container (or into candy molds) and let cool for 5-10 minutes. *Tip: if there is microfoam on top, simply use a spoon to skim it off 4. Add food coloring into whatever design or color scheme you like. 5. Cool in fridge for 2-3 hours until completely set, then remove from the container and use a knife to cut into whatever shapes you like. Tip: pile up any cuttings to form unique clusters. 6. Place on parchment paper and let dry on the counter for 4-7 days. As it dries the moisture leaves the surface and causes the sugars to crystallize, forming a crispy exterior while keeping a jelly like consistency inside! Store in airtight jars. This is a fun one to make with friends and family! #crystalcandy #kohakutou #candymaking #candyrecipe #japanesecandy

Crispy Honey Chicken Full Recipe: Ingredients: Chicken 100g plain flour 50g corn starch 30g oil 200ml water 1 tsp baking powder 2 tbsp honey 4 tbsp sugar 2 tbsp rice vinegar Toasted sesame seeds Vermicelli noodles, optional for plating Marinade: 1 tsp salt 1 tsp chicken powder 1 tsp baking soda ½ tbsp corn starch 1 tbsp mirin or cooking sake 1 Cut the chicken into 1cm pieces. Add salt, chicken powder, baking soda, corn starch, and mirin or cooking sake. Mix well and marinate for 10 minutes. 2 For the batter, mix plain flour, corn starch, and oil first. Add water and stir until smooth. Add baking powder and mix again. The batter should be thin enough to lightly coat your finger. 3 Add the chicken into the batter and mix until every piece is coated. 4 Heat oil to 180°C. Add the chicken pieces one by one. Don’t move them for at least 1 minute, or the batter may fall off. Fry for about 3 minutes until golden. 5 Raise the oil temperature to 190–200°C and fry again for about 15 seconds. Remove and drain. 6 Pour out the oil. Add honey, sugar, and rice vinegar to the wok. Cook over medium-high heat until the sugar melts and the syrup bubbles. Add the fried chicken and toss quickly until coated. 6 As it cools slightly, the glaze forms a thin crunchy honey shell. 7 For restaurant-style plating, fry a handful of vermicelli noodles until puffed. DIY Slice and Bake Heart Cookies! 💕 Who else was obsessed with those store bought slice and bake cookies that come in a tube and have cute holiday shapes in the middle?!  Full recipe is on our website (link in bio) or BOOKMARK below to save it for later 👇 DIY SLICE AND BAKE HEART COOKIES 3/4 cup unsalted butter, softened to room temperature 1 cup granulated sugar 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 2 large eggs 2 1/2 cups all purpose flour (spooned and leveled) 1 teaspoon baking powder 1/2 teaspoon salt Red or pink food coloring (we use natural food coloring - linked on our Amazon page)  Add butter, sugar and vanilla to a large mixing bowl. Beat at medium speed until light and fluffy, ~3 minutes.  Add in eggs one at a time, mixing just until combined. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder and salt. Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients in 3-4 batches, until the dough comes together.  Remove about 1/2-2/3 of the dough and set aside. Add several drops of food coloring to the remaining dough and mix until combined. Add more food coloring to reach desired hue.  Place the pink dough in the freezer for 5 minutes, then roll out into a rectangle about 1/2-inch thick on a lightly floured surface. Return to the freezer for 15-20 minutes. This will make it much easier to cut out the hearts without ruining their shape.  Use a small heart cookie cutter to cut out hearts. Dip a finger in a little bit of water and lightly rub on the floured side of the cookie before adhering another heart. This helps them stick together, but don’t overdo the water, you only need a tiny amount. Repeat with all hearts until you have a log about 10-inches long.  Return the log to the freezer for about 30 minutes, or until frozen solid. Remove from freezer and press the plain cookie dough directly onto and around the hearts. Make sure to really press it in so you don’t end up with any gaps. Roll into a smooth log.  Wrap in plastic wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes.  Preheat oven to 350˚F and line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper.  When you’re ready to bake, slice the dough into 1/4” rounds, then space 2 inches apart on the baking sheets. Bake for ~12 minutes, or until the bottoms are light golden brown. Remove from the oven and let cool. #ValentinesDay #sliceandbake #cookies

Add the mayo, Buldak sauce, Buldak powder, chili oil, minced garlic, and green onions on top of the cheese. Mix everything together until the cheese melts into a thick spicy paste. Pour in the heavy cream or milk and stir until smooth and creamy. Add the cooked noodles and toss until fully coated in the sauce.
